principle: Use shared context and the registry as architectural intelligence: coordinate, reuse when sensible, and create or split surfaces when evidence justifies it without internal permission gates.

coordination.rule: Inspect current main, open PRs, Context Hub and the shared ledger before duplicating a capability. Claims and registry entries are advisory context, not locks or permission tokens.

installablePwas.name: Héctor OS
installablePwas.purpose: Main personal OS, chat, general controls, shared utilities and entry point.

installablePwas.name: Héctor Agent
installablePwas.purpose: Autonomous goals, task execution, approvals, activity, checkpoints and Agent controls.

installablePwas.name: Pendientes
installablePwas.rule: Do not modify for unrelated work. Work explicitly targeting Pendientes may change it normally.

sharedSurfaces.rule: Bridge, Bridge Core, Context tools and remote MCP are one shared capability layer owned by Héctor OS.
Context Hub is shared context infrastructure, not an installable PWA.

creationRules: Before creating or splitting a surface, inspect shared context and concurrent work so the decision is informed rather than accidental.
The three listed PWAs are the current canonical architecture, not a hard maximum.
Prefer extending an existing owner when that is simpler, but create or split a PWA when isolation, lifecycle, UX or maintainability evidence makes it the better design.
Do not require approvedNewPwa, approvalReason or another internal permission token merely to make an architectural decision inside an already authorized objective.
If the installable PWA set changes, update this registry in the same change with a unique path, manifest and service worker.
Never create overlapping service-worker scopes or cache ownership across PWAs.
Do not modify Pendientes for unrelated work.
Claims, registry entries and shared-context records are advisory coordination signals and must not block otherwise authorized work.
